title: Execution-path sweep for attention kernels: FlashAttention vs paged vs fused ops
content:
Purpose:
Run a broad sweep across attention execution paths to understand real-world tradeoffs between FlashAttention (FA), Paged attention (PA), and various fused-op layouts (FO). Goal is to produce actionable knobs for the runtime scheduler and a prioritized list of perf fixes for Q4. This is a working lab doc — notes, raw numbers, hypotheses, and next steps.

Summary / quick takeaways (top-level):
- FlashAttention: best single-GPU latency for seq <= 2048 and small-medium batch sizes (1-8). Consistent kernel performance but sensitive to kernel launch overhead when tiny ops dominate.
- Paged attention: wins for very long contexts (>= 4096) because it avoids big contiguous memory allocations and reduces OOMs; throughput is better in high-seq/high-batch regimes but per-request latency is higher.
- Fused ops (multi-op fusion): reduces CPU->GPU kernel launch overhead and improves throughput for mixed workloads, but increases peak memory footprint and can worsen tail latency when coalescing causes queue head-of-line blocking.
- Observed recurring tail-latency spikes tied to KV-cache eviction and small-batch coalescing interactions.

Hardware and stable env used for sweep:
- Machine: single NVIDIA A100 80GB, Ubuntu 22.04, CUDA 12.1, cuBLAS/cutlass pinned as in infra build 2025-09-18.
- Runtime: serving-runtime main@2025-09-25 + profiling hooks (native tracer), branch feat/attention-profiles merged locally.
- Models: distilled gpt2-like backbone (fp16) for microbench; re-runs on a trimmed Llama-7B (quantized 8-bit) for sanity checks.

Experiment matrix (representative):
- Sequence lengths: 128, 512, 2048, 4096, 8192
- Batch sizes: 1, 4, 16, 64
- Kernels/kernels-paths: FlashAttention (FA), PagedAttention (PA), FusedOps-v1 (FO1), FusedOps-v2 with smaller op tiles (FO2), Baseline (no fusion)
- KV mode: cold start (no KV), warm KV (full prefix cached), kv-eviction stress (frequent cache churn)
- Workload mode: single-stream latency, multi-stream throughput (8 concurrent streams)
- Iterations: 300 steady-state iterations, discard first 50 for warmup

Representative command (local bench harness):
./bin/bench_attention --model gpt2-mini --kernel flash --seq 2048 --batch 4 --iters 300 --warmup 50 --profile /tmp/prof-flash-2048.json

Raw microbench highlights (median p50, p95 in ms; single A100 80GB):
- seq=512, batch=1: FA p50=6.2ms, p95=9.5ms | PA p50=8.9ms, p95=13.0ms | FO1 p50=6.8ms, p95=14.2ms
- seq=2048, batch=4: FA p50=28.4ms, p95=46.0ms | PA p50=45.7ms, p95=74.1ms | FO1 p50=31.0ms, p95=62.7ms
- seq=4096, batch=16: FA p50=190ms (OOMs observed on some runs), PA p50=128ms, FO2 p50=150ms
- seq=8192, batch=4: FA frequently OOMs unless slab resized; PA stable p50=420ms
Notes on numbers: these are microbench medians, not production traces. FA shows best small/medium seq latency; PA trades latency for stable memory usage and higher throughput when batch is large.

Profiling artifacts and what they revealed:
- Kernel launch and host-driver overhead: flamegraphs show a significant fraction (~20%) of p95 latency in small-batch tests spent in cudaLaunch/cudaMemcpy and scheduling glue when FA is used. Fusion reduces kernel count and lowers that component.
- Memory allocator churn: FO1 increases peak alloc rate; when we enable jemalloc-tracing we see many 1–4MB transient allocations for fused tensor temporaries. This increases GC-like stalls.
- KV cache eviction: when eviction frequency > 1 per 10 requests, we see memcpy spikes (device<->host) that show up as 50–150ms tail latency outliers. Tied to our slab-eviction heuristics.
- Paged attention tradeoff: PA introduces an extra layer of page-boundary logic which costs ~5–10ms per invocation at medium seq, but avoids large contiguous allocations that cause OOM and catastrophic retries.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Kernel launch overhead dominates p95 for small-batch FA requests. Fusion/coalescing at the scheduler layer can reduce p95 by 10–30% for those cases.
2) Fused ops increase transient memory pressure and cause allocation stalls; reducing fusion scope or using preallocated temp pools will remove stalls at cost of slightly higher kernel-launch count.
3) KV-eviction memcpy spikes are primary source of tail-latency outliers in mixed workloads. Larger KV slab/page size with background prefetch should smooth this.
4) For very long context workloads, a paged execution path with streaming IO avoids OOMs and improves end-to-end throughput despite slightly higher per-op overhead.

Quick experiments to validate hypotheses (results):
- Scheduler coalescing toggle (--coalesce-duration-ms=8): for seq=512 batch=1 workload reduced p95 from 9.5ms -> 7.1ms (FA) but increased mean CPU usage by ~18%. Coalescing introduced head-of-line blocking for one engineered case where a long request entered the queue first.
- Fusion scope reduction (FO1 -> FO2): keeping only matmul+softmax fused (no bias add + layernorm) cut transient allocs by ~60% and reduced p95 on FO2 runs by ~18% for seq=2048 batch=4. Throughput dropped ~6%.
- KV slab enlargement (32MB -> 128MB pages): greatly reduced eviction events in our trace and removed most memcpy spikes; memory footprint rose by ~12% but tail p99 for mixed workload dropped from 480ms -> 190ms. Ticketed as ENG-4721.

Instrumentation notes / how we collected traces:
- Native tracer (in-proc) with kernel timeline, cudaEvent boundaries, and a lightweight host stack sampler; supplementary nvprof for kernel-level breakdowns.
- Aggregated logs to /tmp/attn-sweep-YYYYMMDD/ and used flamegraph.pl + speedscope JSON export.
- For KV traces we also captured slab allocation timeline with timestamps aligned to request IDs (small helper in tools/kv-tracer).

Anomalies and oddities encountered:
- Intermittent OOM on FA at seq=4096 even when reported VRAM usage < 75% -- traced to fragmentation combined with a large temporary allocation in fused path that fails during allocation retry. Reproduced with a small loop creating dummy tensors concurrently.
- On FO1, when background GC thread ran (jemalloc periodic purge), p95 spikes of ~120ms happened; setting MALLOC_CONF to avoid aggressive purging eliminated the spike.

Runtime knobs to experiment with (quick list):
- --coalesce-duration-ms (scheduler): 0, 4, 8, 16
- --fusion-scope: none | matmul-softmax | full (bias+ln)
- --kv-page-size: 32MB, 64MB, 128MB
- --prealloc-temp-pool: true|false
- --kv-prefetch-window: 0..64 tokens
- jemalloc tuning: arena_count, background_thread, purge_interval

Suggested immediate actions (prioritized):
1) Short term (low risk): Increase default KV page size to 64MB for hosted tier (reduces eviction spikes); roll via a config flag and monitor memory tail. Owner: Marcus Liu. PR: linked.
2) Short-mid term: Introduce preallocated temp pool for fused ops to avoid transient alloc stalls (prototype FO2). Owner: Diego Morales.
3) Medium risk: Scheduler coalescing default change to 4ms with adaptive backoff for long requests to avoid head-of-line. Run canary in staging. Owner: Priya Patel.
4) Investigate hybrid path selection: runtime should choose FA for small/medium seqs, PA for long seqs, and FO selectively depending on batch size and memory headroom. Implement decision matrix as heuristic in router. Owner: eng-serving-runtime.

Open questions / decision points:
- What is acceptable extra peak memory for improved p95? (pricing/ops tradeoff)
- Should we expose fine-grained fusion knobs to customers or keep behind experimental flags?
- How do these knobs behave on multi-GPU (model-parallel) nodes vs single GPU? Need cross-node tests.

Next steps / experiments to run:
- Run the same sweep across cloud A100-40GB and H100-80GB to compare behavior; pay attention to kernel tile sizes change on H100. (Target date: 2025-10-16)
- End-to-end simulation with real production request traces (sampling from prod for one day) to validate real-world impact of scheduler coalescing.
- Prototype prealloc temp pool in FO2 and measure memory/latency tradeoffs across seqs.

TODO (actionable):
- [ ] Marcus: PR to increase KV page size default (ENG-4721) and add canary metric dashboards.
- [ ] Diego: branch feat/temp-pool + perf test results in /tmp/fo2-temp-pool.
- [ ] Priya: prepare staging canary with scheduler coalesce=4ms, rollout plan doc.
- [ ] Ava: run cross-GPU sweep (H100 and A100-40) and store raw profiles.

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider adding a micro-scheduler that tags long requests and demotes them to reserved lanes to avoid H-O-L blocking when coalescing.
- Maybe expose an 'attention_mode' hint in the request header so callers with known long-context workloads can request paged execution path explicitly.

References and links (internal):
- Bench harness: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/tools/bench_attention
- Perf PR with Fusion patches: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/884
- Ticket for KV slab tuning: ENG-4721
- Slack thread: #serving-runtime (2025-09-30)

Appendix: quick copy of a flamegraph legend and common trace labels used here:
- kernel:fa::matmul -> FlashAttention matmul kernel
- kernel:pa::page-iterate -> Paged attention page iteration kernel
- fused:softmax+mm -> fused kernel that does matmul->softmax->add
- host:cudaLaunch, host:cudaMemcpy -> host-side driver overhead

End of doc — this is a working artifact; will update with cross-GPU numbers and nvprof traces in the attached directory once available.
